summary.name: Defining SLOs for services with dependencies (CRE Life Lessons)
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud Blog article from the CRE Life Lessons series on how to define and manage service level objectives (SLOs) for services that depend on other services, each of which may have its own SLOs.
use_cases: Choosing an SLO for a service that has many upstream dependencies
Estimating how dependency outages affect your error budget
Prioritizing reliability risks using a risk analysis spreadsheet
Deciding which dependency risks to mitigate
Setting consequences for SLO violations caused by dependencies
summary.what_it_does: The article explains that services have direct, indirect and structurally implicit dependencies, and that hard, soft and degraded dependencies affect a service differently. It describes complications in combining dependency SLOs, such as correlation between failures, RPC timeouts that differ from dependency SLOs, and retry effectiveness. It recommends setting the SLO top-down from customer needs rather than bottom-up from dependency availability. It then lists mitigation options for dependency risk, such as retries, caching, failover, sharding and graceful degradation, and argues that SLO violations caused by dependencies should still trigger consequences.
notable: Recommends a top-down approach: set the SLO from what customers need, not from what dependencies allow
Distinguishes hard, soft and degraded dependencies and explains why combining dependency SLOs depends on failure correlation
Mentions a risk analysis spreadsheet from an SRECon18 talk by Matt Brown for prioritizing error budget risks
caveats: Gives estimation guidance only; the article states estimates are for prioritization and do not guarantee results
Using published SLOs to model risk tends to overestimate actual risk, as SLOs are usually conservative
